question: Which country among the following declared 'climate emergency' in 2019?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ireland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ireland declared a climate emergency on May 9, 2019, making it the second country in the world to do so.
 
• This declaration was made following a report by the Joint Committee on Climate Action that called for more urgent actions to address climate change.
 
• The motion to declare a climate emergency was passed without a vote in the Irish parliament, showing a broad consensus on the issue.
 
• The declaration acknowledges the severe impacts of climate change and commits to taking more aggressive actions to mitigate its effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate Emergency**

 
 
• A climate emergency is a situation in which urgent action is required to reduce or halt climate change and avoid potentially irreversible environmental damage resulting from it.
 
• The term is often used to convey the urgency of the climate crisis and to push for more aggressive climate policies.
 
• The declaration of a climate emergency typically involves commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, transition to renewable energy, and implement sustainable practices across various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions**
 
 
• Greenhouse gases (GHGs) are gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, leading to global warming and climate change.
 
• The most common GHGs include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and fluorinated gases.
 
• Reducing GHG emissions is crucial to mitigating the impacts of climate change and requires coordinated efforts across industries and governments.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy**
 
 
• Renewable energy comes from sources that are naturally replenished, such as solar, wind, hydro, and geothermal energy.
 
• Transitioning to renewable energy is a key strategy in reducing reliance on fossil fuels and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Investments in renewable energy technologies are essential to achieving long-term sustainability and combating climate change.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Practices**
 
 
• Sustainable practices involve using resources in a way that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
• This includes practices such as reducing waste, conserving water, and promoting energy efficiency.
 
• Adopting sustainable practices across all sectors is critical to ensuring environmental health and economic stability.
